sentence: Methotrexate is an immunosuppressant used for inflammatory conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis and Crohn's disease, and sometimes for cancer.
note: NHS search summary of About methotrexate.

sentence: It is available only on prescription.
The NHS says it calms the immune system to help stop it attacking the body's own cells.
It is not a painkiller, although symptoms may ease as inflammation falls.
Benefit builds slowly, and it can take weeks to months to feel the full effect.
note: Search summary of NHS-affiliated sources said slow, around 3 months; number omitted. DOUBTFUL attribution.

sentence: Methotrexate blocks an enzyme called dihydrofolate reductase, which the body needs to make tetrahydrofolate, the active form of folic acid.
Tetrahydrofolate is needed to build the nucleotides of DNA and RNA.
In inflammatory conditions, how low-dose methotrexate works is less clear.
note: Versus Arthritis: mechanism unclear; trial protocol.

sentence: Proposed explanations include effects on adenosine release, inflammatory signals and the growth of lymphocytes.
When it is used for arthritis and similar conditions, methotrexate is taken once a week, not every day.
note: NRAS: must only be taken once each week; MHRA DSU title.

sentence: Taking it daily by mistake instead of weekly has led to overdoses that were sometimes fatal.
note: SmPC: overdose, sometimes fatal, due to erroneous daily intake instead of weekly.

sentence: In 2020 the MHRA introduced new measures to reduce the risk of fatal overdose from accidental daily dosing.
These include a patient card that prompts weekly dosing, records the chosen weekday and helps people recognise signs of overdose.
The MHRA materials say the card should be carried and shown to clinicians who do not know the person's treatment.
Prescribers are asked to write the weekday in full on the prescription, and pharmacists to write it on the card and the pack.
note: Search summary of MHRA educational materials.

sentence: The NHS says anyone who thinks they have taken too much methotrexate should seek advice from the prescriber or NHS 111 straight away.
note: Search summary of NHS pages. DOUBTFUL: not tied to one page.

sentence: Common side effects listed by the NHS include sensitivity to sunlight, loss of appetite, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headaches and tiredness.
Hair loss can happen and is usually not permanent.
The NHS says to contact a doctor or NHS 111 about yellow skin or eyes, a persistent cough or breathlessness, leg swelling or urine changes.
The same list includes signs of infection and unexplained bruising or bleeding.
The NHS says a severe allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or throat or difficulty breathing, needs a 999 call.
Methotrexate may increase the risk of liver or lung problems, particularly at high doses, which is why regular checks are done.
Folic acid is usually prescribed alongside it, because methotrexate can interfere with how the body takes up B vitamins.
Versus Arthritis says blood tests of the blood count, kidney function and liver function are needed before starting.
Tests are more frequent at the start and become less frequent once treatment is steady.
NHS monitoring guidance also lists hepatitis B and C and HIV screening and a chest X-ray among the checks before starting.
The same guidance notes that a downward trend in results can point to toxicity even when values are still in range.
Methotrexate may increase the risk of liver or lung problems, particularly at high doses, which is why regular checks are done.
Because methotrexate affects the immune system, infections may be more likely.
The NHS says to ask a doctor urgently about an infection, or after contact with someone who has chickenpox or shingles.
note: Search summary of NHS pages. DOUBTFUL.

sentence: The NHS says methotrexate is not recommended in pregnancy, as it can cause birth defects.
Anyone taking it who wants to become pregnant is advised to speak to their doctor.
If pregnancy happens during treatment, the NHS advises speaking to a doctor as soon as possible.
Shared-care protocols advise effective contraception during treatment and for some months afterwards, and the length of time differs between sources.
note: Protocols say 3 and 6 months; numbers omitted.

sentence: Guidance on exposure through the father is less settled, so the specialist advises on timing.
note: Search summary of rheumatology protocol. DOUBTFUL.

sentence: The NHS says that if methotrexate causes vomiting or severe diarrhoea, contraceptive pills may not protect against pregnancy.
Breastfeeding is also listed among reasons methotrexate may not be suitable.

sentence: The NHS lists allergy to methotrexate, severe liver or kidney disease, a blood disorder and current infection among reasons it may not be suitable.
